title: Authentication contract is the sole authority for login semantics
context: Historical login semantics in ../react are scattered across controllers and middleware, with no single normative source.
decision: The USF authentication contract is the sole normative source for login semantics; historical implementations are evidence only.
consequences: Login behaviour must be derived from the authentication contract, not from historical controllers.
Historical ../react login code is retained as evidence and lineage, never as live authority.
invariants: Login semantics are defined exclusively by the authentication contract.
permittedChanges: The authentication contract may be extended by a recorded decision that preserves existing invariants.
forbiddenDrift: Implementations must not reintroduce login semantics that contradict the authentication contract.
Historical source behaviour must not be promoted to live authority.
aiAlignmentRules: Do not infer login semantics from historical implementation structure.
Stop and report if a requested change would contradict the authentication contract.
rationale: A single normative authority prevents semantic drift across implementations.
description: Architecture decision establishing the authentication contract as the sole authority for login semantics, with historical source treated as evidence.
aiGuidance: This ADR is binding only while accepted; treat its invariants and forbidden drift as authoritative.
